requirement:
A result of the `habeas` line-range form, `list_files`, `outline`, `ripgrep`,
`ast_grep`, or `references` whose serialized JSON exceeds 32 KiB MUST be
returned in pages. Each page MUST hold whole entries of the result's arrays, such
as inputs, matches, nodes, or sites, with its accompanying definitions, in the
result's order, and MUST NOT exceed 32 KiB unless a single entry does, which
then forms a page of its own. Every paged result MUST include:

```text
page: {
    total_entries: Integer,
    returned_entries: Integer,
    next: String?,
}
```

`next` MUST be an opaque token when entries remain and null on the last page.
While entries remain, the page MUST also include a `note` saying that more
entries remain and that `next_page` with `next` returns them. The
harness MUST expose a `next_page({ token: String })` tool returning the following
page of the same result, in the same shape. Pages MUST be kept only until the
assessment that requested them finishes; an unknown token, including one from
another assessment, MUST return an explanatory tool error. A result within the
limit MUST be returned whole, without `page`. Only inputs on pages delivered to
the model MUST be recorded under {cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`.
rationale:
**Verdict.** The paging implementation matches the requirement except for one boundary case: a result that is within the limit but gets paged anyway. That case is untested.

**What the code does.**
- `src/authoring/pages.rs#impl[ResultPages]/fn[deliver]` decides whether to return a result whole or in pages. `fn[paginate]` splits the entries into consecutive pages of whole entries. It counts the commas, page fields and accompanying definitions, so a page stays within `PAGE_LIMIT` (32 KiB). A single entry over the limit forms a page of its own.
- `Listing` covers the result arrays for `habeas`, `list_files`, `outline`, `ripgrep`, `ast_grep` and `references`. `src/authoring/tools.rs#const[REFERENCE_ARRAYS]` orders the reference arrays as definitions, then sites.
- Every paged result carries `page` with `total_entries`, `returned_entries` and `next`. `next` is a random 16-hex-character token, or null on the last page. A page with more entries after it also carries `PAGE_NOTE`, which says to call `next_page` with `next`. I read "the page MUST also include a note" as the note sitting inside the `page` object; the code and tests do that.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[dispatch_paged]` exposes the `next_page` tool. `fn[definitions]` advertises it with a single `token` argument.
- `ResultPages` is created inside `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]`, so pages live only for that assessment. An unknown token, including one from another assessment, returns the "unknown page token … valid only in the assessment …" error.
- `Listing::inputs`, `delivered` and `ResultPages::deliver` record, for each page, only that page's inputs plus its own definitions. That satisfies the citation of `requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`.

**Tests that cover it.**
- `large_listings_and_outlines_page_whole_entries_in_order` covers paging of `list_files` and `outline`: whole entries, in order, each page within the limit, and the page fields.
- `paged_inputs_carry_their_definitions_and_deliver_only_their_own_inputs` covers `habeas`: definitions placed per page, delivery limited to a page's own inputs, the unknown-token error (a second `ResultPages`, standing in for another assessment, and a bad token through `next_page`), and re-asking a token.
- `an_entry_exceeding_the_limit_forms_a_page_of_its_own_and_small_results_stay_whole` covers the oversize entry and the whole-without-`page` case.
- `reference_results_page_definitions_then_sites` covers `references`.
- `not_listed_comes_on_the_first_page_within_the_page_limit` covers the extra key on the first page.
- `only_inputs_on_delivered_pages_are_recorded` covers recording only delivered inputs end to end.

**Gap: a result within the limit is not always returned whole.**
- `ResultPages::deliver` returns a result whole only when `whole.to_string().len() + NOTE_RESERVE <= PAGE_LIMIT`. `NOTE_RESERVE` is the redaction note's length plus 16 bytes.
- A result whose serialized JSON is at most 32 KiB but within `NOTE_RESERVE` bytes of it is therefore paged. This happens even when nothing is redacted.
- The requirement says a result within the limit MUST be returned whole, without `page`. The same window can produce a single "page" with `next` null and a `page` field.
- No test covers this boundary. The tests use clearly small or clearly large results, and `all_pages` even asserts more than one page.
- The text states the limit as 32 KiB with no allowance for a redaction note that may never be added.

Because of this unmet MUST and its untested boundary, the requirement is not fully satisfied.
